DOMAIN DIMENSION PANELS

Five realms. Five arcs. Clear every skill card in a session to claim its XP — progress when you finish with good form and only moderate fatigue, not by the calendar.

📐 ORIGIN TRIAL — YOUR BASELINE

Open from day one. Retest every 6 weeks. Four numbers, ten minutes, full rest between each — this is a measurement, not a workout.
TIER I
Origin Arc — Beginner

MIDORIYA DOMAIN

Inspired by: early Izuku Midoriya · pre-training Rock Lee · Asta

▸ Focus — Learning the patterns · building base capacity
  • Trains: the six foundation patterns — push, pull, squat, hinge, brace and gait — at their easiest leverages: wall and incline push-ups, chair rows, box squats, glute bridges, knee planks.
  • Goal: three sessions a week you actually finish, with clean form and 1–3 reps left in the tank. At this stage the adaptation is the consistency — tendons and technique lag muscle by months.
  • Deliberately absent: no failure sets, no intensity techniques, no equipment. Nothing here should leave you unable to train two days later.
3× / WEEK — FULL BODY
📜 WEEKLY PROTOCOL — FULL BODY 3×/WK
  • Schedule: e.g. Mon / Wed / Fri — always ≥1 rest day between sessions.
  • Each session: clear the cards shown for today, in any order (big moves first works best). The TODAY selector above the grid decides which cards those are.
  • Zero equipment: floor, wall and a sturdy chair. Nothing else is required at this tier.
  • Progression rule: hit the prescription with 1–3 reps still in reserve, grade it honestly, evolve (▲) after 3 clean clears. The cards handle progression — you do not need to add reps yourself.
  • Deload: every 4th week — half the sets, easy pace, same movements.
🔥 WARM-UP — 5 MIN, EVERY SESSION
🧊 COOL-DOWN — 3 MIN

"You can become a hero." — All Might

TIER II
Training Arc — Novice

TANJIRO DOMAIN

Inspired by: Saitama's original 100-100-100-10km routine · Tanjiro's endurance drills

▸ Focus — Weekly volume · aerobic base
  • Trains: the same patterns at harder leverages, split upper/lower across 4–5 sessions, plus running. This is where sustained pulling work starts.
  • Goal: tolerate real weekly volume without breaking down, and build an engine alongside the strength. Work capacity is the target, not peak output.
  • Watch: weekly pull sets must at least match push sets. Skipping the pull card is how posture debt accumulates — and floor pulling caps out, which is what the Toji side arc is for.
4–5× / WEEK
📜 WEEKLY PROTOCOL — UPPER / LOWER 4×/WK
  • Schedule: Upper / Lower / rest / Upper / Lower / rest / rest.
  • UPPER days: Push-Ups · Pull path · Core · Plank · Mountain Climbers.
  • LOWER days: Squats · Hinge (Single-Leg Glute Bridge) · Burpees · Run / Jog.
  • Never skip the pull card — it is the only thing holding your posture together against all that pressing. Match your sets: as many weekly pull sets as push sets, minimum.
  • Pull is the bottleneck. Floor and towel pulling works, but it caps out. A doorway bar (~$30), a park bar or a railing closes the gap faster than anything else here — run the TOJI SIDE ARC alongside this tier for the bar work. It is optional, never gated, and does not replace your tier.
  • Progression rule: leave 1–2 reps in the tank on all sets except the last; evolve (▲) after 3 clears.
  • Deload: every 5th week — half sets, skip the burpees.
🔥 WARM-UP — 5 MIN, EVERY SESSION
🧊 COOL-DOWN — 3 MIN

"No matter how devastated you may be, keep moving forward." — Tanjiro Kamado

TIER III
Gravity Arc — Intermediate

GOKU DOMAIN

Inspired by: Goku’s Gravity Chamber · King Kai’s Planet · Saiyan Survival Training

▸ Focus — Turning volume into intensity
  • Trains: harder leverages, 3-second lowering tempo on LIGHT days, and plyometrics on HEAVY days. Tempo — not extra reps — is the main overload lever from here on. The Ki Hinge card is the tier's only dedicated hamstring work.
  • Goal: convert Tier II's volume into force output and rate of force development, so Tier IV's near-max work builds you instead of injuring you.
  • Cost: highest joint stress in the app. Alternating HEAVY/LIGHT and the 5th-week deload (no plyos at all) are load-bearing rules, not suggestions.
4–5× / WEEK — FULL BODY
📜 WEEKLY PROTOCOL — FULL BODY 4–5×/WK
  • Alternate HEAVY and LIGHT days — never two heavy days back to back.
  • HEAVY (Gravity Chamber): plyometrics first while fresh, then max-leverage strength.
  • LIGHT (King Kai’s Planet): same movements at a 3-second lowering tempo — this is your main overload lever now, not extra reps.
  • HEAVY, after the plyos: the Ki Hinge card — leg curls and RDLs. Plyos and squats are all knee; this is the only card in the tier that loads the hamstrings.
  • Day 5 (optional): Full Body Finisher (Saiyan Survival) — one conditioning block, not two.
  • Why this tier exists: Tier II built volume. Tier III turns it into intensity through leverage and speed, so Tier IV’s near-max work does not break you.
  • Progression rule: evolve (▲) after 3 quality clears — same engine as every domain.
  • Deload: every 5th week — half sets, no plyometrics at all, LIGHT-day tempo work only. This is the highest joint-stress tier in the app; the deload is not optional here.
  • Pull is the bottleneck. Floor and towel pulling works, but it caps out. A doorway bar (~$30), a park bar or a railing closes the gap faster than anything else here — run the TOJI SIDE ARC alongside this tier for the bar work. It is optional, never gated, and does not replace your tier.
🔥 WARM-UP — 5 MIN, EVERY SESSION
🧊 COOL-DOWN — 3 MIN

"Power comes in response to a need, not a desire." — Goku

TIER IV
Legendary Arc — Advanced

SAITAMA DOMAIN

Inspired by: Saitama at full power · Guts · Baki · peak All Might

▸ Focus — Maximum strength · high-frequency conditioning
  • Trains: push / pull / legs across 5–6 sessions — wall handstand push-ups, the pistol path, the Nordic hinge path, sprints and long runs. Near-max leverage work on every pattern.
  • Goal: peak strength and engine at the same time, measured against the Boss Trial as a benchmark you retest roughly monthly — not as a daily dose.
  • Cost: the highest total volume here. Run it as the PPL split with the TODAY selector — three or four cards a day, not all ten. See the note under the quote for why.
5–6× / WEEK
📜 WEEKLY PROTOCOL — PUSH / PULL / LEGS 5×/WK
  • Schedule: Push / Pull / Legs+Core / rest / Push (volume) / Pull+Engine / rest.
  • PUSH: Push-Up Variations · Wall Handstand Push-Ups.
  • PULL: Towel Door Rows · Floor Pull Battery — zero equipment, towel and a latched door only.
  • Honest caveat: floor pulling is the weakest link in any no-gear plan. If you can reach a park bar or railing, swap in chin-ups — it closes the gap faster than anything else here, and the TOJI SIDE ARC below is built around exactly that.
  • Weekly ratio check: this tier has two pressing cards (Push-Up path, Wall HSPU) and two pulling cards. Count them — weekly pull sets must be ≥ weekly push sets. Both PUSH days are the ones that break the rule; if you add a press set, add a pull set on the same day.
  • LEGS+CORE: Pistol path · Hinge (Nordic path) · Burpees · V-Ups / L-Sit path.
  • ENGINE: Sprints · Plank · easy run.
  • Progression rule: quality over grind — evolve (▲) after 3 clean clears; never chase reps with broken form.
  • Deload: every 5th week — or run the 3-week Boss prep instead (see below).
🔥 WARM-UP — 5 MIN, EVERY SESSION
🧊 COOL-DOWN — 3 MIN

"100 push-ups. 100 sit-ups. 100 squats. 10km. Every single day." — Saitama

Saitama's routine is fiction. It is a joke in the source material — the punchline is that an absurdly ordinary program produced an absurd result. Run as written, at 5–6 sessions a week, this tier's ten cards are 37 working sets plus sprints: 100 V-ups and 75 burpees in a session, with Nordic negatives stacked on top of that fatigue. That is not an advanced program, it is an injury schedule — and the hamstring is where it lands first.

This tier is therefore run as the PUSH / PULL / LEGS split the protocol always prescribed — use the TODAY selector above the grid. Three or four cards a day, not ten. The sprints are conditioning and sit outside the session. "Every single day" is the story, not the dose.
👊 BOSS BATTLE — SAITAMA'S TRIAL
100 PUSH-UPS · 100 SIT-UPS · 100 SQUATS · 10KM — in a single day

A benchmark, not a daily grind — retest every ~4 weeks and watch it get easier. Your first clear breaks the seal on the MASTERY ARC below.

Swap the 100 sit-ups for 100 hollow rocks or V-ups if your lower back objects — that is a lot of loaded spinal flexion in one day. And run the 10 km last or on a separate half of the day; on legs pre-fatigued by 100 squats is where form breaks down.

📈 3-WEEK PREP PROGRAM — run this before your first attempt
  • Week 1: 4 rounds of 15 push-ups · 15 sit-ups · 15 squats, then 4 km easy — 3 days, spread out.
  • Week 2: 4 × 20 each + 6 km — 3 days.
  • Week 3: 4 × 25 each + 8 km — 2 days, then 2 full rest days before the Trial.
  • Trial day: fresh, fed, hydrated. Break sets as needed — the clock is the whole day.
TIER V
Mastery Arc — Elite

ROCK LEE DOMAIN

Inspired by: Rock Lee opening the Inner Gates · Baki's obsession with technique · skill over brute volume

▸ Focus — Skill over volume
  • Trains: handstand, the planche path, the one-arm path, pistols and the L-sit / V-sit progression — short, fresh sets with full 2–3 minute rests.
  • Goal: positions and control, not reps. Skill work is practice, not a workout: you stop well before failure, because a fatigued rep teaches the wrong pattern.
  • Structure: an undulating hard → medium → easy weekly wave. The skill consolidates during the easy weeks, so do not delete them.
3–4× / WEEK — SKILL PRACTICE
📜 WEEKLY PROTOCOL — UNDULATING 3–4×/WK
  • Day 1 — SKILL (fresh): Handstand · Planche path — short quality sets, stop well before failure.
  • Day 2 — STRENGTH: One-Arm path · Pistol path · Hinge (RDL → Nordic path) — low reps, full 2–3 min rests.
  • Day 3 — ENGINE + CORE: L-Sit / V-Sit · 10 km path.
  • Day 4 (optional) — light skill practice + mobility only.
  • Weekly wave: hard week → medium week → easy week — repeat. Skill grows in the easy weeks.
  • Pull is the bottleneck. Floor and towel pulling works, but it caps out. A doorway bar (~$30), a park bar or a railing closes the gap faster than anything else here — run the TOJI SIDE ARC alongside this tier for the bar work. It is optional, never gated, and does not replace your tier.
🔥 WARM-UP — 5 MIN, EVERY SESSION

SIDE ARC
Sorcerer Killer — Optional Path

TOJI DOMAIN

Inspired by: Toji Fushiguro · peak-human, zero-power archetypes

▸ Focus — Closing the pulling gap · bar-based strength
  • Trains: chin-ups, inverted rows and negatives — the vertical and horizontal pulling that four tiers of floor and towel work cannot reach — plus a legs/shoulders day and a dedicated core day.
  • Goal: fix the one deficit every zero-equipment tier shares. Back and biceps are the ceiling on a no-gear plan, and a bar removes it.
  • Requires: a doorway bar (~$30), a park bar or a railing. Swaps are listed in the protocol if you do not have one yet — weaker, and honest about it.
  • Placement: optional and never gated. Run it beside your current tier or in place of it; it sits outside the five-tier chain.
3× / WEEK — STRENGTH SPLIT · NEEDS A BAR
📜 WEEKLY PROTOCOL — 3× / WK SPLIT
  • This one’s optional. It sits outside the five-tier path — not above it, beside it. Run it instead of a tier, or alongside one. Nothing here is gated.
  • Equipment: doorway pull-up bar (~$30), sturdy chair, two towels. The bar is the whole reason this arc exists — four tiers of floor pulling can only take your back so far.
  • Schedule: Day 1 push+pull · Day 2 legs+shoulders · Day 3 core — a rest day between each.
  • Day 1: Sorcerer Killer · Blade Grip.
  • Day 2: Null Domain · Inverted Spear · Heavenly Restriction.
  • Day 3: Assassin’s Core · Instant Kill.
  • Off days: Manji Sprint — sprints on active rest days, walk daily.
  • Progression rule: same engine as every domain — evolve (▲) after 3 quality clears. The source routine calls for sets to failure; this app doesn’t, and the evolution ladder already handles overload.
  • No bar yet? Swap Chin-Ups → Towel Door Rows 4×15, Inverted Rows → Feet-Elevated Towel Rows 4×12, Negative Pull-Ups → One-Arm Towel Rows 4×8/side, Windshield Wipers → Alternating Side Plank Reach 4×16. Weaker, and honest about it.
  • Source: movement selection adapted from Bodybuilding.com’s calisthenics strength routine (Heather Eastman, NSCA-CPT).

♾️ ENDLESS ARC — PAST THE MASTERY ARC

Bodyweight training has exactly six ways to add load. The FORM ladder is one of them. Here are the other five, and what to do when the ladders run out.
📐 TEMPO NOTATION — what 30X1 means
  • First digit — lowering. 3 = three seconds down, under control.
  • Second digit — pause at the bottom. 0 = no pause. 2 = a two-second dead-stop, which removes every bit of stretch reflex.
  • Third — the lift. X = explosive intent, as fast as you can move it. A number means that many seconds.
  • Fourth — pause at the top. 1 = one second, no resting on locked joints.
  • So 30X1 = 3s down · no pause · explode up · 1s at the top. The Gravity Arc's "3s tempo" cards are 30X0.
⚔️ Progression rule: move to the next tier when you can complete a full session with good form and only moderate fatigue at the end — not by the calendar.

Levels do not gate anything. XP, the board below and the badges are a trophy case — no tier is ever locked behind a level, because grinding XP cannot give you the strength to hold a pistol squat. There is exactly one real lock in this app: the Mastery Arc opens on your first Saitama’s Trial clear — and even that can be overridden if you know what you are doing.

FLEXIBILITY ARC

Range is a prerequisite, not a bonus. Half the Mastery Arc is gated by mobility, not strength — train it on rest days, where it costs you nothing.

SUPPORT
Flexibility Arc — Prerequisite Work

RANGE DOMAIN

Unlocks: pistol squats · L-sit · planche lean · handstand push-ups

3× / WEEK — REST DAYS · ~10 MIN
ACTIVE RANGE Adds a 10s isometric push at end range to every hold. Passive range you can't control doesn't transfer — this is what converts it into usable range.
Dose: roughly 5 minutes per muscle group per week is where the evidence lands. Total weekly volume matters more than how you slice it — 2×60s three times a week gets you there. Moderate discomfort, never pain; pushing harder does not speed this up.
Most of your early progress is stretch tolerance, not tissue length. Your nervous system stops guarding the range. That's why it feels neurological, and why it reverses if you stop. Expect 4–8 weeks for meaningful change. Nothing useful happens in a week.
Two things stretching won't fix. Bony restriction — hip socket depth and femur angle cap squat depth for some people, and bone doesn't stretch. A hard block or a pinch at the front of the hip is structural; stop chasing it. And nerve tension — if a hamstring stretch reads as tingling or a line running down the leg, that isn't a short muscle, and aggressive stretching makes it worse.

⚖️ THE CUT

How fat loss actually works — and what training is really for
A deficit decides how much you lose. Training decides what you lose. Nothing here spot-reduces the gut — abdominal fat is usually the last to go, and that is normal.

1 · LIQUID CALORIE AUDIT

One day. Every drink with calories in it — juice, soda, the oat milk, the beers, the two sugared coffees. This is a screen, not a lecture: if it comes back near zero, you are done with this step forever.

2 · STEP TARGET — 8–10K/DAY

The reason is recovery cost, not calorie burn: walking competes with your training for almost nothing, and running competes for a lot. If you work a physical job or shift work, you may already be over target — check before adding.

3 · RESISTANCE TRAINING

You are already doing this — it is the rest of the app. Go to your tier.

Why it works is worth getting right. You will read that lifting burns fat because muscle is metabolically active at rest. The mechanism is real and the magnitude is trivial: muscle runs about 6 kcal per pound per day against roughly 2 for fat, so five pounds of hard-won new muscle buys you about 30 kcal a day. That is a third of an apple.

The real reason: the same deficit without training sheds a meaningful share of muscle along with the fat. The same deficit with hard training preserves the muscle and takes the fat. That is the entire case for lifting while cutting, and it is a far stronger one than the metabolism story.

The retention signal depends on proximity to failure, not on how many sessions you log. This is why the CLEAN / GRINDY / FAILED grade on every card matters — five sessions a week at an effort level that never approaches failure sends no retention signal at all.

RATE & TARGETS

Loss rate cap0.5–0.75% BW/wk
Protein targetrun the calculator
Weigh-in methodweekly average

There is no fast way. Rate is capped by how much fat you are carrying, and pushing past the cap trades away the muscle you are training for.

RECOVERY & RULES

The part that decides whether any of the training above works
😴 SLEEP — the primary variable
  • 7+ hours. Under 6, expect strength loss regardless of how good the programming is. There is no supplement, split or intensity technique that substitutes for this.
  • Soreness is not a progress metric. Its absence is not a failed session, and its presence is not a good one — it mostly tracks novelty.
  • Two consecutive sessions of declining performance on the same card means under-recovered. Deload early; the app will usually have flagged it first.
🚑 INJURY & REGRESSION RULES
  • Sharp, localized or joint-line pain: stop the card. Not "push through". This is the one rule in the app with no exceptions.
  • Fine: muscle burn, general fatigue, delayed soreness for a day or two.
  • Not fine: nerve symptoms (tingling, numbness, shooting pain), pinching at end range, and anything still there past 48 hours.
  • Regressing (▼) is a normal programming action, not a failure and not an XP loss. Deliberately dropping a form to hold clean technique is the ladder working as designed.
  • Pain that persists: see a professional. This app is a training tool, not a clinician.
🏃 CARDIO — zones, and how much is too much
  • Zone 2 — conversational pace, you could hold a sentence. Builds the aerobic base, low recovery cost. This is most of your cardio.
  • Intervals / sprints — high cost, competes directly with lifting. Cap hard conditioning at 2 sessions per week when you are lifting 4 or more.
  • Sprints go first in a session, while you are fresh — never after burpees.
  • Plyometric cap: ≤100 foot contacts per session, ≤2 plyometric sessions per week. The load meter above each grid counts them for you.
🧰 SUBSTITUTIONS — when the program does not fit the room
  • Every card has swaps in the dropdown under it — tagged by the constraint they solve: apartment noise, shoulder, hamstring, no anchor, joint pain.
  • A swap is not a step down the ladder. Your form index and clean-clear count carry across untouched.

CONDITIONING & ACCESSORIES

The work that sits outside the session — and the gaps the tiers never covered

WEEKLY CONDITIONING

Steps are the default. Running is optional, and stays optional — the endurance identity of the Tanjiro and Saitama tiers is there for anyone who wants to chase it, without taxing everyone else's recovery.

DAILY ACCESSORIES — 5 MINUTES

Grip is the limiter on every hanging progression, and dead hangs double as shoulder decompression. Neck work changes how a physique reads more than almost anything else per minute spent, and is near-universally skipped.

ASYMMETRY TEST

Everything advanced here is unilateral — pistols, one-arm work, single-leg hinges. A side difference over 20% is how those get you hurt. Test on single-leg glute bridge or a pistol to a chair, max reps each side.

    PRIVACY & DATA

    Your save never leaves this browser unless you export it.
    📄 PRIVACY POLICY — PLAIN ENGLISH
    • What we collect: nothing. There is no server, no account, no analytics, no ads, no cookies.
    • Where your data lives: in your browser’s localStorage, on your device only.
    • External requests: zero. The fonts are embedded in this page as data URIs — nothing is fetched from Google or anyone else. Load the page once and it works offline, forever, with no network traffic at all.
    • Your rights (GDPR / CCPA): access & portability = Export buttons above · erasure = Delete Everything. Both work instantly because the data was only ever yours.
    • Cloud sync: a static site has no server to sync to — by design. Use the encrypted backup + any cloud drive for the same result.
    • Backups: browsers can wipe localStorage (storage pressure, clearing site data, private tabs). Export regularly — the app will remind you.
    • Offline: this is a single self-contained file with every font and image embedded and a Content-Security-Policy of default-src 'none'. There is no service worker because there is nothing to cache and nothing to fetch — save the file and it works in a basement with no signal, permanently. Progress photos are stored in a separate slot so exports stay small.

    Honest caveat: fasting protocols are a tool, not magic. If you have any underlying health conditions or a history of disordered eating, check with a doctor before starting an aggressive cut or fasting schedule.
